AbstractText.Label: RATIONALE
AbstractText.content: Extremely sharp angular spinal deformity of healed tuberculosis can be corrected by vertebral column resection (VCR). However, the VCR techniques have many limitations including spinal column instability, greater blood loss, and greater risk of neurologic deficit.

AbstractText.Label: PATIENT CONCERNS
AbstractText.content: We described a new spinal osteotomy technique to collect sharp angular spinal deformity in Pott disease. A 52-year-old woman presented with back pain and gait imbalance.

AbstractText.Label: DIAGNOSIS
AbstractText.content: The kyphosis of healed tuberculosis was diagnosed based on history and imaging examinations.

AbstractText.Label: INTERVENTION
AbstractText.content: A new posterior VCR was designed to treat this disease.

AbstractText.Label: OUTCOMES
AbstractText.content: The neurological function improved from Japanese Orthopedic Association scale 3 to 7. The back pain and neurological function were significantly improved. The Oswestry Disability Index decreased from 92 to 34. There was also a significant decrease in back pain visual analog scale from 9 to 2.

AbstractText.Label: LESSONS
AbstractText.content: For cases with extremely severe Pott kyphotic deformity, the technology of modified VCR offers excellent clinical and radiographic results.

Article.ArticleTitle: Vertebral column decortication for the management of sharp angular spinal deformity in Pott disease: Case report.
